- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or shows strong bearish momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect risk aversion bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially when sentiment is neutral or mixed — apply downward correction in next 3-5 periods.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting — forecast should be adjusted upward 1-2 periods ahead of true trend.
- Mean reversion bias: if model is consistently above 75% of recent 10-day average, reduce forecast; if below, increase — especially when sentiment is weak or volatile.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — apply smoothing filter or lagged sentiment weighting (e.g., 3-period moving average of sentiment) to dampen noise.
